text.arabic_uthmani: ذُوقُوا۟ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ

words.gloss_range: imperative plural command to taste or experience directly; locally a punishment command rather than neutral tasting
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, trying, and knowing by contact; the local command selects forced experiential verification of punishment, not ordinary food-tasting

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the named trial as direct object
long vowel in the imperative surface

words.prose: {{ar:ذُوقُوا۟}} ({{tr:dhūqū}}) opens as a bare second-person plural imperative, so the punishment speech lands as an enacted command to the whole addressed group, not as a report about what will happen. The verb makes the trial something known by contact: {{ar:فِتْنَتَكُمْ}} ({{tr:fitnatakum}}) is to be tasted as bodily, unavoidable verification. That sensory force answers the fire-testing scene of 51:13, moving from outside description into direct address. The command also belongs to a recurring punishment-imperative pattern (6:30, 8:35, 32:20, 54:48), while the local syntax keeps the payoff specific: present tasting is tied to their prior state without making distributional co-occurrence an extra local sense. Its short hard opening and lengthened {{ar:و}} ({{tr:ū}}) make the command feel both abrupt and inescapably prolonged.

topics.headline: abrupt plural imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah begin as an immediate command addressed to the culpable group, not as narrated description.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a 2mp imperative with implicit subject; no speaker formula or softening particle intervenes.

topics.headline: tasting as contact-verification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is forced into firsthand sensory contact, so judgment becomes empirically undeniable.
topics.reason: The direct object is the trial, and the root range supports tasting/trying by experience as the active local image.

topics.headline: punishment formula with prior-state pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this command as part of a Quranic punishment-command idiom while still reading the local object and prior-state clause as the controlling grammar.
topics.reason: Cross-corpus formula and co-occurrence evidence support recognition of a punishment-command pattern, but they do not add a separate object or override the local command-object frame.

topics.headline: fire-scene becomes direct address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the shift from 51:13 as watched fire-testing into 51:14 as speech from inside the punishment scene.
topics.reason: The adjacent ayah supplies the fire-testing scene, and the imperative changes the discourse from third-person report to second-person command.

topics.headline: abrupt sound texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the compact command as rough and prolonged, matching forced experience rather than a softened invitation.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound rows are compatible with the short imperative surface and do not conflict with grammar.

words.gloss_range: your trial, ordeal, or testing; locally the direct object of tasting and possessed by the addressed group
words.root_gloss_range: testing, trial, affliction, seduction, and fire-assaying; the local fire context keeps trial and assay imagery active while not reducing the word to literal metallurgy alone

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperative that governs the noun as object
possessive suffix attached to the trial noun

words.prose: {{ar:فِتْنَتَكُمْ}} ({{tr:fitnatakum}}) names the thing the command forces them to taste, so the opening is not vague suffering but their own trial as a direct object. The attached {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:kum}}) makes the ordeal possessively definite: they are the ones undergoing it, and the wording lets their own conduct remain implicated in why it is theirs. The root’s trial range is sharpened by 51:13, where the same root appears in the fire-testing scene; the noun now turns that process into a possessed object of experience. Its fire-assay image lets the punishment expose and test, not merely hurt, while local grammar keeps the sense to moral ordeal rather than literal metalwork alone. Broad co-occurrence with being-state language can support the link to what they had been doing, but a general divine-name co-occurrence adds no separate local payoff here.

topics.headline: possessed object of tasting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the trial is not anonymous; it is grammatically made their own object of experience.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the noun the direct object of the command and marks the suffix as possessive.

topics.headline: trial as fire-assay
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the fire scene as a testing and exposing process, not only as pain.
topics.reason: The root range supports trial/assay imagery, and 51:13 supplies the immediate fire-testing context.

topics.headline: passive process becomes possessed noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 51:13’s passive fire-testing return in 51:14 as the noun they must taste.
topics.reason: The same root crosses the ayah boundary from passive verb to possessed verbal noun.

topics.headline: trial tied to prior state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the trial with the prior-state clause, while the local noun remains governed by the tasting command.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence supports a relation between trial and prior being, but local syntax keeps the immediate role as direct object.

topics.headline: broad divine-name cooccurrence
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: No local divine-name surface or syntactic relation is present for this row to add a reader-facing payoff beyond the retained trial topic.
topics.reason: The row cites a broad co-occurrence pattern rather than a local word relation in 51:14.

topics.headline: abrasive trial texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the hard stop texture reinforce the compressed harshness of the named ordeal.
topics.reason: The sound observation fits the surface and is a small but coherent local payoff.

words.gloss_range: near masculine singular demonstrative pointing to the present punishment/trial and opening an identity statement

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: matching relative pronoun that defines the demonstrative
later pronominal reprise of the pointed object
nearby trial noun included in the demonstrative reference range

words.prose: {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) points to the punishment as present and near, making what they had treated as future judgment into this immediate object of address. As the subject of a verbless identification clause, it equates the present suffering with what the relative clause will define; no extra copula is needed for the identity to land. Its masculine singular form binds with {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}), while its reference can gather {{ar:فِتْنَتَكُمْ}} ({{tr:fitnatakum}}), the punishment scene, and the demanded object together. The demonstrative therefore pivots the ayah from the command to taste into the ironic explanation, and the later {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihī}}) reprises the same pointed reality inside the hastening clause.

topics.headline: proximal identity statement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment pointed out as present reality and identified with the thing formerly demanded.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support a masculine singular demonstrative opening a nominal identification clause.

topics.headline: referent gathered and bound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trial, punishment scene, relative definition, and later pronoun are held around one pointed object.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the demonstrative reference as locally ambiguous but strongly links the later pronoun to the demonstrative-relative head.

topics.headline: pivot from command to irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah’s architecture: experience first, pointed identification second, accusation third.
topics.reason: The demonstrative stands between the imperative-object clause and the habitual-past relative clause, making it the structural hinge.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun defining the demonstrative through the following clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: relative content reaching to the ayah end
closing verb of the relative clause

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) turns the pointed {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) into a defined object: this is the thing that you had been seeking to hasten. The relative pronoun opens scope all the way through {{ar:تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ}} ({{tr:tastaʿjilūna}}), so the explanation is not detached from the demonstrative but grammatically completes it. Its masculine singular concord locks the clause to the pointed punishment; whether read as predicate or as close modifier, the payoff is the same bridge from present reality to past demand. The liaison from {{ar:هَٰذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) into {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) audibly supports that dependence rather than a hard restart.

topics.headline: relative clause as definition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment is defined by their prior demand, not merely followed by an explanatory aside.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the relative clause as completing the demonstrative nominal sentence.

topics.headline: concord with stable parse range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the predicate/modifier parse range without losing the main point that the relative clause belongs to the demonstrative.
topics.reason: The exact syntactic label may be predicate or modifier, but masculine singular concord and clause structure block a loose detached reading.

topics.headline: bridge from now to then
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the relative pronoun collapse the gap between present punishment and past habitual demand.
topics.reason: The relative connector stands between the proximal demonstrative and the past habitual clause, with recitational liaison matching the syntactic dependence.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural perfect auxiliary; with the following imperfect it frames the hastening as prior habitual conduct
words.root_gloss_range: being, existing, becoming, and formation; locally the auxiliary use selects past-state framing while allowing the prior state to feel consequential

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperfect predicate governed by the auxiliary
same addressed group now commanded to taste
second-person plural suffix on the auxiliary

words.prose: {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) is the temporal hinge of the relative clause. With {{ar:تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ}} ({{tr:tastaʿjilūna}}), it makes the hastening a prior habitual state, not a single past request, so the present command to taste answers a settled pattern. Its attached {{ar:تُمْ}} ({{tr:tum}}) keeps the same addressed plural moving through the ayah: taste, your trial, you were, you were hastening. The root’s being and becoming range can make that old state feel formative of the present reversal, while local grammar keeps {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) functioning as an auxiliary rather than a full lexical claim of creation. Distributional links with tasting, trial, and haste support the verdict-scene cohesion, but the local payoff remains the habitual-past frame.

topics.headline: habitual past frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the hastening as repeated prior conduct, making the punishment a response to a pattern rather than one outburst.
topics.reason: Attachment explicitly identifies the following imperfect as the predicate of the auxiliary, and QAC marks the perfect 2mp form.

topics.headline: same accused you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one addressed group held responsible from the opening command through the closing accusation.
topics.reason: The auxiliary and main verb share 2mp marking, matching the imperative and possessive suffix earlier in the ayah.

topics.headline: being-state as formative background
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels their former mode of being as the background that formed the reversal, while the auxiliary grammar stays primary.
topics.reason: The root range includes being and formation, but the local construction uses the verb as an auxiliary with an imperfect predicate.

topics.headline: cohesion with tasting, trial, and haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see prior being tied to tasting, trial, and haste as a verdict-scene pattern without adding a new sense to the auxiliary.
topics.reason: Distributional evidence supports cohesion among the roots, but does not override the local auxiliary function.

topics.headline: nasal continuity into the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the auxiliary and closing verb as one continuous accusation.
topics.reason: The sound observation follows from adjacent surfaces and supports the clause-level continuity.

words.gloss_range: preposition with masculine singular pronoun; locally the governed complement of the hastening verb, referring back to the pointed punishment

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: antecedent head resumed by the pronoun
verb completed by the prepositional phrase
prepositional prefix in the compact complement

words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihī}}) routes the object of hastening through a prepositional complement: they were seeking the hastening of this, not merely acting in a generally hurried way. The attached pronoun sends the reader back to {{ar:هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:hādhā alladhī}}), so the same punishment pointed out as present is carried into the closing accusation. Because the complement stands before {{ar:تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ}} ({{tr:tastaʿjilūna}}), this very object is foregrounded before the action is named. The broader range of {{ar:بِـ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) can leave a concerning or causal feel around their impatience, but the local construction keeps the primary role as the governed complement of the Form X verb. Its compact preposition-plus-pronoun form makes dependency and reference happen at once.

topics.headline: governed object of hastening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the hastening is directed at this object, not a vague habit of rushing.
topics.reason: Attachment identifies the phrase as the prepositional complement of the closing Form X verb.

topics.headline: concerning or causal pressure of the particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the object as what their impatience revolved around, while the complement function remains the selected local role.
topics.reason: The broader particle range is compatible as secondary pressure, but local syntax selects complement scope rather than instrumentality.

topics.headline: pronoun reprises the pointed punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one object from demonstrative pointing to pronominal complement inside the accusation.
topics.reason: Attachment strongly links the suffix to the demonstrative-relative head and treats it as a resumptive reference.

topics.headline: fronted demanded object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demanded object is placed before the verb, keeping this punishment prominent.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase precedes the verb it complements inside the relative clause.

topics.headline: compact attachment into the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the object-marker lean straight into the hastening verb.
topics.reason: The surface compresses proclitic and pronoun, and it directly precedes the closing verb.

words.gloss_range: you were seeking or demanding hastening; locally Form X imperfect under {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) marks repeated demand for acceleration
words.root_gloss_range: haste, hurry, acceleration, and seeking to hasten; the local Form X selects requesting acceleration rather than simple speed or actual control over timing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: auxiliary that makes the action habitual past
prepositional complement naming what was hastened
long plural ending at the ayah close

words.prose: {{ar:تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ}} ({{tr:tastaʿjilūna}}) is the final disclosure of the ayah’s irony: the thing they now taste is what they had repeatedly demanded be brought sooner. Under {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}), the imperfect makes the demand habitual, not a single impatient utterance. Form X makes them seekers of acceleration rather than controllers of time; with {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihī}}), the verb is about demanding this object, not merely being quick. The same root appears in Quranic punishment-demand settings (6:57-58, 8:32, 10:50-51, 27:46, 29:53-54, 46:35), and this surah returns to haste at 51:59, so the closing word sounds like a motif of ironic fulfillment. Broader root associations can make haste feel like reckless immediacy, including the calf scene (20:83-88), but the local word does not name that scene; it selects demanded acceleration. The long closing {{ar:ون}} ({{tr:ūna}}) and the shared ending with 51:13 let the word for haste linger instead of rushing away.

topics.headline: habitual demand under the auxiliary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands that the accusation concerns repeated demand, not a one-time request.
topics.reason: The verb is an imperfect predicate under {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}), supporting habitual-past force.

topics.headline: seeking acceleration, not controlling it
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees their agency as demanding the judgment sooner, while actual timing remains outside their control.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form X, and the governed {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihī}}) complement supports seeking hastening of something external.

topics.headline: same accused group to the end
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same plural addressees held in view through the ayah’s final word.
topics.reason: The plural ending matches the earlier second-person forms and carries subject agreement.

topics.headline: punishment-demand motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the closing accusation as part of a wider pattern where demands for judgment are answered by judgment.
topics.reason: The supplied references and distributional profiles place the Form X root in repeated judgment-demand contexts, including a later surah-local haste thread at 51:59.

topics.headline: closing ironic reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reaches the final word and discovers that the tasted punishment is exactly the demanded object.
topics.reason: The verb closes the relative clause and provides the defining action for {{ar:هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:hādhā alladhī}}).

topics.headline: reckless immediacy as background
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may feel haste as concrete reckless immediacy, while the local verb remains demand for acceleration rather than a calf reference.
topics.reason: The broader root family can color the haste field, but the local Form X verb and complement block importing the calf scene as a referent.

topics.headline: lingering closure of haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final word for haste linger in a drawn cadence, even echoing the ending of 51:13.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound rows are surface observations tied to the final word and adjacent ayah ending.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The demanded proof becomes tasted experience.** `ذ و ق/B002` supplies undergoing/testing, `ف ت ن/B001` assay and B004 ordeal, and `ع ج ل/B001` seeking before its time. The deictic *hādhā* reverses the earlier temporal question into present encounter. I infer **premature demand for verification -> verification arriving as ordeal**. Their epistemic challenge is answered through embodied experience.
2. **Haste is reversed into an inescapable present.** `ع ج ل/B001` contrasts immediate with deferred; `ك و ن/B001` marks their continuing prior state. The later repeated prohibition on hastening (51:59) closes the pattern. I infer **habitual acceleration -> appointment made immediate against the demander**. This is a temporal reversal, not merely rebuke.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:59 repeats the haste root but restores deferment, revealing 51:14 as the completed reversal in which premature demand has become immediate experience.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Hastened information becomes embodied verification.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `ذ و ق/B002` is “experiencing and testing something”; fixed `ف ت ن/B001` is “assaying by trial”; fixed `ع ج ل/B001` is “hastening and bringing forward.” **Structural cue:** 51:12 asks when, 51:13 turns the answer into fiery assay, and this ayah binds tasting to what was hurried; 51:15–19 then present a contrary chain of protection, receiving, restrained sleep, forgiveness, and due sharing. **Role and abduction:** haste pulls the event forward, assay tests, and tasting internalizes the result; I infer that their demand for premature disclosure is answered by participation rather than explanation. **Reading change:** the imperative is not only “suffer”; it makes the sought proof inseparable from the seekers’ own sensory experience.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:15–19’s sequence of protected reception and measured giving exposed a contrary mode of encounter, making haste look like a failed way of receiving what comes.
